primitives.name: OSS Integration Boundary
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Legal / License Boundary Allowed: study docs, use APIs, self-host in an isolated lab, and write original GSE integration code.
primitives.assumptions: Open-source materials are studied in isolation; no direct code reuse occurs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When integration moves beyond documentation into application code.

layer2.mapping: The boundary enforces a structural isomorphism between external OSS and internal GSE operational semantics.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of codebase isolation and API usage compliance.

primitives.name: Sandboxed Implementation Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Start in docs or a sandbox and only move into app code after explicit approval.
primitives.assumptions: Implementation begins in non-production environments with controlled access.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upon transition from documentation to application-level code.

layer2.mapping: Derives kernel behavior from sandboxed execution logs and approval traces.
layer2.telemetry: Audit trail of sandboxed activity and approval timestamps.

primitives.name: Rollback Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Security Boundary No secrets, production data, customer PII, proprietary method docs, payment data, or production source keys.
primitives.assumptions: All artifacts are ephemeral and do not persist sensitive or production-related data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upon failure or rejection of an implementation.

layer2.mapping: Derives rollback capability from deterministic artifact states and versioned documentation.
layer2.telemetry: Revertibility metrics of document and branch changes.

The primitives define a logical separation between exploration (docs/sandbox) and implementation (code), enforcing a dual-state workflow. The rollback protocol ensures reversibility, while the integration boundary prevents unauthorized code reuse. These elements form a closed-loop system where decisions are made based on risk tolerance and operational fidelity. The failure mode arises when this boundary is crossed without approval, leading to potential security or compliance breaches.
